/*
 * Cut Up Any Clothing
 * aspctt - 23.08.2026
 * Generated by tools/generate_cut_clothing.py, do not edit by hand.
 *
 * Build 42 decides whether a garment can be cut into strips from a tag, and that tag
 * is separate from the FabricType saying what the garment is made of. The two disagree
 * constantly: underwear, socks, bandanas, scarves and gloves all declare a fabric and
 * were never tagged, so the game knows they are cotton and still will not let you cut
 * them up. Shoes have it worse and carry no fabric at all.
 *
 * Reopening an item merges rather than replaces, and a Tags value is added to the set
 * rather than overwriting it, so everything that makes these garments work is untouched.
 *
 * The tags cannot be switched off from here, because a lua tag patch lands after the
 * recipes have already cached their inputs. The sandbox switch is the recipes' OnTest
 * instead, reading the same list this pass writes to qolc_cut_clothing_items.lua.
 *
 * Rubber footwear is deliberately absent: Shoes_FlipFlop, Shoes_Wellies, Shoes_TireSandals.
 */
module Base
{

	item Tshirt_EMD

	/*
	 * The mapper decides what the crafting screen predicts, and nothing else. What a
	 * garment actually turns into is settled by RecipeCodeOnCreate.ripClothing, which
	 * reads the garment's FabricType and looks the strips up in
	 * ClothingRecipesDefinitions. The mapper is never consulted for that.
	 *
	 * So this is not what makes leather boots give leather strips. They would do that
	 * on the strength of their FabricType alone. It is here because vanilla's mapper
	 * lists eleven jackets and pairs of trousers by name and defaults everything else
	 * to denim strips, so without it the screen promised denim and handed over leather.
	 *
	 * Reopening the recipe adds to that mapper rather than replacing it. Verified in the
	 * jar: LoadOutputMapper calls getOrCreateOutputMapper, which returns the existing
	 * mapper when one is already registered under that name, and PreReloadScripts runs as
	 * one pass over every script before any file is parsed rather than per block. So
	 * vanilla's eleven stay and these are added to them, and a leather item the game adds
	 * later still arrives on its own.
	 *
	 * No icon is set. One was, scissors, on the reasoning that a recipe producing two
	 * different things cannot have one honest picture of its output. It is held back
	 * until the icon is actually seen to be wrong in game: with the mapper above in
	 * place a leather garment now reports leather strips rather than denim, which was
	 * the whole of the complaint, and replacing a correct icon with a tool would be a
	 * loss. See tools/generate_cut_clothing.py to put it back.
	 *
	 * OnTest is the sandbox switch. It runs per candidate item and refuses the ones this
	 * mod tagged when the option is off, leaving everything vanilla allows untouched.
	 */
	craftRecipe RipDenimClothing
	{
		OnTest = Recipe.OnTest.QolcCutClothing,

		itemMapper fabricType
		{
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Belt2,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Briefs_Hide,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_FingerlessLeatherGloves,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_FingerlessLeatherGloves_Black,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_FingerlessLeatherGloves_Brown,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_LeatherGloves,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_LeatherGlovesBlack,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_LeatherGlovesBrown,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Gloves_LeatherWrap,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_ArmyBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_ArmyBootsDesert,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Black,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_BlackBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Bowling,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Brown,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CowboyBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CowboyBoots_Black,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CowboyBoots_Brown,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CowboyBoots_Fancy,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CowboyBoots_SnakeSkin,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_CrudeLeatherFootwear,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Fancy,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_HideBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_HikingBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_LeatherWrap,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_RidingBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Sandals,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_Strapped,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Shoes_WorkBoots,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Trousers_DeerHide,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Trousers_Hide,
			Base.LeatherStrips = Base.Underpants_Hide,
		}
	}

	/* Cotton tears by hand and has one fixed output, so only the switch is needed. */
	craftRecipe RipClothing
	{
		OnTest = Recipe.OnTest.QolcCutClothing,
	}

	/*
	 * Wallets, which are containers rather than clothing. They cannot join the two
	 * recipes above at any price: RecipeCodeOnCreate.ripClothing casts its input to
	 * Clothing and asks for a FabricType, and a container has neither. So this is a
	 * recipe of its own, with a fixed output and no OnCreate to go wrong.
	 *
	 * IsEmpty because a wallet holds things, and shredding one with the car keys still
	 * inside would be a poor reward for tidying up.
	 */
	craftRecipe QolcCutWallet
	{
		timedAction = CutClothing,
		time = 60,
		Tags = InHandCraft;RemoveResultItems,
		OnTest = Recipe.OnTest.QolcCutClothing,
		category = Tailoring,

		inputs
		{
			item 1 tags[base:scissors;base:sharpknife] mode:keep flags[MayDegradeLight;Prop1;IsNotDull],
			item 1 [Base.Wallet;Base.Wallet_Male;Base.Wallet_Female;Base.Wallet_Hide] mode:destroy flags[IsEmpty;ItemCount],
		}

		outputs
		{
			item 1 Base.LeatherStrips,
		}
	}
}
